subject: Hosting commitment appendix and private peering timeline
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novamed.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: NovaMed Security <compliance@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify hosting boundaries, KMS residency and peering timeline

Rohan —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG/SOC-2 evidence pack we need explicit confirmation on a few items for our legal/compliance review:

- Confirmation that customer data for NovaMed will be stored and processed within the US region (us-east-1 equivalent) for the Private deployment variant.
- Details on the VPC peering/private endpoint model you support (shared VPC vs. dedicated peering), and whether cross-region egress is possible/restricted by default.
- KMS key residency: can we provision customer-managed keys that are owned and controlled by NovaMed, and will those keys be exclusively stored in the US region?
- Proposed timeline for a private peering test (connectivity + perf) and a KMS rotation test window; we prefer a two-week window in April if possible.

Please attach any short appendix or runbook we can include in the questionnaire. If you can indicate owners and a recommended date range for the test, that will help us lock calendars.

Thanks —
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Security Ops, NovaMed
oliver.grant@novamed.com

[attachment: nova-sig-questions-v2.xlsx]

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novamed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify hosting boundaries, KMS residency and peering timeline

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, and a small appendix attached with the runbook bits for your pack. See below for owners and a proposed test window.

1) Region residency: For Redwood Private deployments we support a single-region hosting model for your tenant. For the configuration we discussed, all data and model inference traffic for NovaMed will be kept in the US region (we can map to your preferred AZs).

2) Networking: We support dedicated VPC peering (one-to-one) for Private customers. That gives you direct peering into the Redwood subnet; we do not require shared tenancy. By default cross-region egress is blocked for Private deployments unless explicitly configured as part of a multi-region DR plan.

3) KMS: You can supply customer-managed keys (CMKs) via your KMS (we integrate with mainstream KMS providers). Keys can be provisioned and restricted to the US region; we do not replicate those keys outside the region unless you request cross-region replication.

4) Timeline and owners:
   - Private peering connectivity test: proposed window Apr 11–15 (owner: Kimberly Park, Network PM).
   - KMS rotation/test: proposed window Apr 18–22 (owner: Marissa Cole, Security Eng).

Attachments: redwood-hosting-appendix.pdf — includes short block diagram, default firewall rules, and data-flow for CMKs.

Next steps: If those windows are OK, we’ll open the SUP ticket and schedule a pre-test sync (30 min) the week prior.

Thanks,

Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Rohan / team —

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. Quick clarifications:

- Confirmed: Apr 11–15 for peering test and Apr 18–22 for KMS rotation look fine from our side.
- We will provision a CMK in our KMS and provide the ARN; can you confirm the exact IAM role and policy we need to grant Redwood to use the key for envelope encryption?
- For the peering test, please include a short perf checklist (expected RTT, throughput targets) so our infra team can instrument accordingly.

Can we have the SUP ticket and a link to the runbook by Friday, Mar 12? That gives us enough time to prepare.

Oliver

Oliver —

All set. We opened SUP-2048 and dropped the initial runbook into the Drive folder (link below). Attached is a one-page IAM snippet and the perf checklist for the peering test.

Action items we own before Apr 11:
- Kimberly: scheduling and pre-test connectivity checklist; will run a brief topology review with your infra on Apr 8.
- Marissa: KMS IAM policy template and rotation playbook; will share the ARN example and policy by Mar 12.
- Stephanie: will own the test-day rollback plan and monitoring queries for the run.

We will not enable any cross-region egress unless NovaMed signs the multi-region addendum; the default tenant configuration is single-region only.

Please confirm if Apr 11 is a hard hold for peering or if you want us to treat it as flexible within Apr 11–15.

Thanks — we’ll aim to have the SUP ticket details and the IAM snippet to you before end of day Mar 12.

— Rohan
